claims.text: The freshly synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution has high intrinsic lattice distortion caused by random elemental mixing.
Annealing at approximately 200°C for 1 hour under an inert atmosphere will partially relax lattice strain in PtPdRhRuIrOs.
The proposed annealing treatment can relax strain without significant particle sintering or phase separation.
The catalyst surface state is the main factor governing activity and selectivity under the specified ethanol-oxidation conditions.
Local lattice strain in PtPdRhRuIrOs modulates its d-band center.
Changes in the d-band center alter the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
High-entropy mixing creates significant local lattice distortions in the as-synthesized catalyst.
The as-synthesized lattice distortions place the d-band center at a position favorable for strong adsorption of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Partial relaxation of lattice distortion by annealing shifts the d-band center.
The annealing-induced d-band shift weakens adsorption of key oxygenated intermediates.
Weaker binding of oxygenated intermediates lowers the catalyst's ethanol-oxidation activity.
Weaker binding of oxygenated intermediates changes the distribution between partial and complete ethanol-oxidation products.
At a given potential, the annealed catalyst will have lower catalytic current density than the unannealed catalyst.
Annealing will alter product selectivity, including a possible change in the acetaldehyde-to-acetic-acid ratio.
The proposed effects should hold only when annealing does not induce sintering or phase separation.
Particle size and exposed surface facets may change the balance between beneficial strain and excessively strong adsorption.
